newsitem.title: UK: US Treasuries in London recover, consumer data due.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries in London recover, consumer data due.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday continued to recover from a knee-jerk sell-off sparked by comments by Japanese Prime Minster Ryutaro Hashimoto overnight, with strong flows into the market ahead of Tuesday's U.S consumer confidence data, traders said.

Hashimoto said in New York that Japan might be tempted to switch its holdings of U.S. Treasuries into gold reserves if the U.S. did not make efforts to maintain exchange rate stability, but Japan's Finance Ministry said on Tuesday it had no intention of selling U.S. Treasuries.

"We're a little firmer from late trade in Asia, continuing a recovery of sorts from the Hashimoto-induced shock-horror sell-off in late U.S. trade," said Charles Quigly, U.S. bond salesman at Chase in London.
The market awaits consumer confidence data at 1400 GMT. A Reuter poll forecasts the index, currently at 28-year highs, will come in at 126.3 for May, off April's level of 127.1.
The benchmark long bond was quoted at 99-05 at 0940 GMT, for a yield of 6.689 percent, 2/32 Tokyo's close of 99-03, and firmer on New York's close of 98-31.
September T-bond futures were down 2/32 at 112-03 in automated trade.
But while analysts said firm U.S. May consumer confidence data would dent the market initially, it would prompt a jump back in, they said.

"It will be a buy-on-dip mentality," said Adam Chester, bond strategist at Yamaichi International Europe in London. "If we get a setback people will use that as an opportunity to get back into the market, with rate perception still very much benign."
The market is also looking to the sale of $15.5 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday, with an $11.5 billion five-year auction to follow on Wednesday.
